headline: Cancer single-cell and transcriptomic studies dominate the cell death label, not death…
label: cell death death
summary: 22 items (19 published, 3 preprints), mostly cancer scRNA-seq and prognostic-signature studies; cell death is not the stated focus of any item.
synthesis: Items under this label (22: 19 published, 3 preprints) are predominantly cancer transcriptomic and multi-omics studies rather than investigations of cell death mechanisms. Recurring methods include scRNA-seq atlases, scATAC-seq integration (colorectal, bladder, endometrial, hepatocellular carcinoma), bulk-to-single-cell cross-validation, and prognostic gene signatures, such as the six-gene mechanosensitive signature for colorectal liver metastasis and the 4-gene ECM signature in prostate cancer. No item summary states cell death as its focus; the closest links are tumor epithelial state programs and survival-associated signatures. Cross-platform concordance is a recurring caveat: weak osteoblast signature concordance in osteosarcoma, and no FDR-passing genes in one colorectal liver metastasis single-cell reanalysis. The rise (ratio 3.23; 7-day star gain zero; no code or industry items) is descriptive only, and the items do not establish a cause.
